audit.title: Getting Historical Data
audit.summary: This is a solid, code-rich how-to page for reading Chainlink historical feed data via `getRoundData`, with complete Solidity/JavaScript/Python examples and real addresses. Its biggest strength is code completeness and structural chunkability; its biggest opportunity is discoverability — the page has zero JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no dates, and no symptom/question-phrased headings, so it under-retrieves against the queries devs actually type ("getRoundData reverts", "how to get historical price data"). The canonical API (`getRoundData`) is present but arrives late in each section rather than in the first liftable sentence, leaving it vulnerable to generic parametric answers.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased headings and a troubleshooting block
recommendations.where: new H2 near end + rename existing sections
recommendations.issue: no headings match "how do I…" or error-string queries; revert behavior hidden in prose.
recommendations.change: Add an H2 "How to get historical price data in Solidity" and a "Troubleshooting" H2 with entries phrased as symptoms: "`getRoundData` reverts / returns empty", "Why is my `roundId` not incremental?", "`updatedAt` is 0 — round not complete". Answer each in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: devs and agents query by symptom; question-titled sections win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle`, canonical URL, and last-updated date
recommendations.issue: JSON-LD: 0 blocks; canonical MISSING; dateModified absent.
recommendations.change: Emit a `TechArticle` block with `headline`, `about` ("Chainlink Data Feeds historical data"), `programmingLanguage` (Solidity/JavaScript/Python), canonical `https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/historical-data`, and a visible `dateModified`.
recommendations.why: structured metadata + freshness signals raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust for agents choosing sources.

recommendations.title: Lead each section with the canonical API in the first liftable sentence
recommendations.issue: "As shown in the decentralized model, the consumer contracts call the proxy contract…" delays the answer.
recommendations.change: Open with: "To read historical Chainlink feed data, call `getRoundData(uint80 roundId)` on the `AggregatorV3Interface` proxy. `roundId` values are not incremental — you must know a valid one." Then explain the model.
recommendations.why: puts the canonical API in the chunk an engine lifts first, resisting generic "loop from round 1" priors.

recommendations.title: Name the common-but-wrong pattern as an explicit Don't
recommendations.issue: "roundId is NOT incremental" lives only in a code comment.
recommendations.change: Add a visible callout: "Don't assume `roundId` starts at 0 or increments by 1 — proxy roundIds encode a phase in the high 64 bits. Compute valid roundIds using the phase formula below."
recommendations.why: explicitly naming the wrong assumption blocks the model from synthesizing the generic incrementing-loop answer.

recommendations.title: Quantify the deviation/heartbeat table
recommendations.issue: "trigger an update every *X* minutes / hours" — no numbers.
recommendations.change: Give a concrete example row, e.g. "ETH/USD on Ethereum Mainnet: 0.5% deviation, 3600s heartbeat," with a link to the feed's live parameters.
recommendations.why: quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

recommendations.title: Fix the "can can" typo and add a `getRoundData` one-line definition
recommendations.where: *Historical rounds* first paragraph; *getRoundData return values* heading
recommendations.issue: "historical data can can be stored"; no crisp definition of the function.
recommendations.change: Correct the typo; add "`getRoundData(roundId)` returns the answer and timestamps recorded for a specific past round." before the bullet list.
recommendations.why: clean prose is independently rewarded; a self-contained definition is verbatim-liftable.

recommendations.title: Show expected output for the runnable examples
recommendations.issue: examples call `getRoundData` but show no returned shape.
recommendations.change: Add a comment showing the expected tuple, e.g. `# (roundId, answer, startedAt, updatedAt, answeredInRound)` with sample values.
recommendations.why: expected output lets agents validate correct usage without executing.

antiPatterns: Minor typo: "historical data can can be stored."
Placeholder/uppercase comment noise in code (SPDX/THIS/EXAMPLE/HARDCODED) flagged by scan — harmless boilerplate, not keyword stuffing; no change needed.
Key gotcha ("roundId is NOT incremental") buried in code comments rather than surfaced as retrievable prose.
No stale-content risk visible, but absence of any date means freshness is unverifiable.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is listed in it.
Site-level JSON-LD/schema injection and a consistent `dateModified` cadence are platform concerns beyond this single page.
CLI should pass raw `<head>` next run — head metadata could not be verified, so the metadata score reflects the served HTML only.
